MCALESTER, OK / ACCESS Newswire / November 4, 2026 / Glo Tan… Family-owned 3PL serving the ports of Seattle, Tacoma, Los A… NEW YORK, Nov. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ichnos Glenmark Innovation, Inc. (IGI), a global clinical-stage biotechnology company developing Multispecific™ therapeutics in oncology, today announced that updated clinical data from the Phase 1 study of ISB 2001 (ABBV-2001) in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) will be presented as an oral presentation at the 68th American Society of Hematology (ASH) Annual Meeting. “With longer follow-up from dose escalation and initial results from dose expansion, ISB 2001 (ABBV-2001) continues to demonstrate robust efficacy and tolerability in heavily pretreated patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma,” said Lida Pacaud, M.D., President and Chief Executive Officer of IGI. “These results represent an important milestone in the development of this first and only trispecific T-cell engager targeting CD38 x BCMA x CD3. Together with our partner, AbbVie, we remain focused on advancing ISB 2001 (ABBV-2001) as a potential new treatment option for patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM).” ISB 2001 (ABBV-2001) Oral Presentation (abstract link): First- and only-in-class CD38 x BCMA x CD3 trispecific T-cell engager ISB 2001 (ABBV-2001): Updated Phase 1 (TRIgnite-1) study data demonstrate robust efficacy and tolerability in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) Presenter: Binod Dhakal, M.D., Medical College of Wisconsin (MCW) Date & Time: Saturday, December 12, 2026, 4–4:15pm CST Room: La Nouvelle C at the Ernest N. Morial Convention Center, New Orleans Session: 654. Multiple Myeloma: Pharmacologic Therapies: The March of Immunotherapy ISB 2001 (ABBV-2001) is an investigational first- and only-in-class trispecific T-cell engager targeting CD38 and BCMA on myeloma cells and CD3 on T cells that is in development for the treatment of relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM). Engineered using IGI`s BEAT® Multispecific Platform, ISB 2001 (ABBV-2001) coordinates dual-antigen tumor recognition with immune engagement through T cells within a single molecular architecture. IGI and AbbVie formed an exclusive global licensing agreement for the trispecific in July 2025. ISB 2001 (ABBV-2001) is being evaluated in multiple myeloma through the Phase 1 TRIgnite-1 study and a Phase 1/2 combination study. IGI is a global, fully integrated clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing innovative biologics in oncology. Headquartered in New York, NY, IGI is advancing a robust pipeline of novel, first-in-class Multispecifics™ aimed at addressing complex diseases and treating patients holistically. Powered by its proprietary BEAT® technology platform, IGI is committed to delivering breakthrough curative therapies to improve and extend the lives of patients battling hematological malignancies and solid tumors. title: AbbVie Director Jennifer Davis Resigns From Board - Gotrade
content: Gotrade News - Jennifer L. Davis has resigned from the board of directors of AbbVie Inc. (ABBV) effective Monday, November 2, 2026, according to AbbVie's Form 8-K filing with the SEC. The filing says she is leaving in light of her recent appointment as Chief Executive Officer at Align Technology, Inc. Regular-session close on November 2, 2026, New York time. Prices and changes: Yahoo Finance, cross-checked against the closing price on Nasdaq.com. Market cap: that close times the shares outstanding on the latest 10-Q or 10-K cover (SEC EDGAR). On Wednesday, October 28, 2026, Davis, a Class II director of AbbVie, notified the company's Board of Directors of her intent to resign from the board, effective Monday, November 2, 2026, according to the filing. AbbVie reported the departure under Item 5.02 of the Form 8-K, in a filing that came out at 4:05 p.m. ET on Monday. The filing gives her recent appointment as Chief Executive Officer at Align Technology, Inc. as the reason for her decision. Align's own Form 8-K sets out that appointment: its board named Davis CEO-elect and a director effective Monday, November 2, 2026, and President and CEO effective Thursday, December 31, 2026, when Joseph M. Hogan retires from that role. According to Align's filing, Davis has served on AbbVie's board since 2023. Before joining Align, she was Chief Executive Officer, Health Care of The Procter & Gamble Company from 2022 through June 2026. The change is at the board level: the filing reports the resignation of one director and does not report a change to any of AbbVie's officers. AbbVie states in the filing that her resignation is not the result of any dispute or disagreement with AbbVie on any matter relating to its operations, policies or practices. The filing does not name a replacement for her seat, and it does not say whether the board plans to fill the seat or change its size. What to watch next: AbbVie pays its quarterly cash dividend of $1.73 per share on Monday, November 16, 2026, to stockholders of record at the close of business on Thursday, October 15, 2026. Management highlighted the continued momentum of key products like SKYRIZI, RINVOQ, and VRAYLAR, each delivering double-digit revenue increases. CEO Rob Michael emphasized that "nine key products delivered double-digit growth," with particular strength in immunology and progress in new indications for neuroscience therapies. The quarter's performance also benefited from newly approved treatments and advancements in product delivery, reflecting strong commercial execution. Looking forward, AbbVie's outlook is shaped by anticipated launches, expanding indications, and ongoing pipeline development. Management expects the recent subcutaneous induction approval for SKYRIZI in Crohn's disease and upcoming launches for RINVOQ in vitiligo and alopecia areata to contribute meaningfully to future growth. CFO Scott Reents indicated that new product launches and continued uptake in neuroscience, including the Parkinson's therapy JUVMO, will help sustain momentum. Management also sees opportunities in advancing combination therapies and new developments in oncology and obesity. Management attributed the quarter's performance to volume gains in immunology and neuroscience, product lifecycle expansion, and execution on new launches. Immunology volume expansion: SKYRIZI and RINVOQ both saw strong growth across indications, with SKYRIZI prescription trends holding up despite new competition. The subcutaneous induction approval in Crohn's disease is expected to further strengthen SKYRIZI's position and accelerate new patient share in coming quarters. Neuroscience product momentum: The company's neuroscience segment was driven by VRAYLAR, UBRELVY, Qulipta, and the recent launch of JUVMO for Parkinson's disease. Management noted that JUVMO, with its differentiated profile, is expected to gradually ramp up as commercial and Medicare coverage expands. Oncology pipeline progress: AbbVie highlighted positive developments in multiple myeloma (etentamig) and large B-cell lymphoma (Epkinly), with regulatory submissions underway and approvals anticipated next year. Management described these assets as underappreciated by the market and important contributors for future revenue. Aesthetics stabilization: While overall aesthetics sales declined slightly, BOTOX Cosmetic revenues grew modestly. Management observed early signs of stabilization in the aesthetics segment and is rolling out Boey, a new fast-acting toxin, in Europe and Canada. Strategic M&A and pipeline investments: The acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics added differentiated assets in dermatology and respiratory diseases, while business development remains focused on augmenting depth in core therapeutic areas rather than pursuing large-scale deals. AbbVie's guidance centers on continued growth in immunology and neuroscience, new indication launches, and execution of its advancing pipeline strategy. New indication launches: Management expects the launch of SKYRIZI subcutaneous induction in Crohn's disease and U.S. launches of RINVOQ in vitiligo and alopecia areata to drive further growth. These new indications are anticipated to expand the addressable patient base and reinforce market share in key therapeutic areas. Pipeline milestones and regulatory events: Anticipated approvals for etentamig in multiple myeloma and Epkinly in large B-cell lymphoma are seen as major near-term catalysts. Additionally, positive interim data from various late-stage trials, particularly in immunology and neuroscience, could accelerate future launches and revenue streams. Market access and payer dynamics: Management identified strong payer access for new launches as a key to sustaining growth, with low single-digit rebate concessions expected. However, external factors such as regulatory changes, competitive pressures, and evolving reimbursement frameworks present ongoing risks. AbbVie completed the Apogee Therapeutics acquisition during the quarter. Apogee Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharma focused on immunological and inflammatory diseases, complementing AbbVie’s core portfolio with several therapies in development. Other growth avenues include the Neurosciences and Oncology segments, which have promising pipelines of their own, in addition to today's drivers. The Neurosciences segment is supported by Vraylar and Botox Therapeutic, along with Ubrelvy and Qulipta. Oncology is also contributing, although growth has been more modest. Looking ahead, the company has approximately one dozen promising therapies in advanced testing across segments, including expanded treatments for Skyrizi and Rinvoq. AbbVie expects those two drugs to generate more than $32 billion in combined sales in 2026. AbbVie reported third-quarter results, with revenue of $17.4 billion, up 10.3% year over year and just above consensus. Sales were driven by a 16.3% increase in Immunology, including solid gains in Skyrizi and Rinvoq, a 19.4% increase in Neurosciences, and a 0.8% increase in Oncology. Aesthetics, including Botox Cosmetic, fell 1.4% but remains a cash driver. Margin news is more impressive, with costs and acquired in-process research and development (IPR&D) milestones far less than last year, resulting in wider gross and operating margins. Adjusted operating margin came in at nearly 49%, up almost 18 percentage points, sufficient to drive triple-digit increases in the GAAP and adjusted earnings figures. Adjusted earnings per share of $3.82 grew 105%, outperforming MarketBeat’s consensus by about nine cents and enabling management to raise guidance for the second time this year. The company significantly raised its adjusted earnings per share (EPS) target, setting the low end at $13.95, in line with consensus, and the high at $13.99. ABBV could perform near the high end of its forecast or potentially outperform it, given Q3 strengths and developments, including expanded approvals for key drugs. AbbVie’s investment appeal lies in its growth but centers on profitability, cash flow, and its capacity for capital returns. Share buybacks aren’t the primary driver but help keep the share count steady while dividends are distributed. The current dividend yields approximately 2.41% in early November, more than double the broad market average, with above-average distribution growth also forecasted. AbbVie has a Dividend King-level dividend growth record, including its history with Abbott Laboratories. Analysts' response to Q3 results and guidance included several price target increases. As it stands, the 30 analysts tracked rate the stock as a Moderate Buy with an 80% Buy-side bias and no Sell ratings logged, forecasting a slight correction at the consensus, but the trend matters. Consensus is up versus last year, last quarter, and early October, providing a tailwind. Institutional investors have also been buying ABBV in 2026, with institutional ownership now exceeding 70% of shares. This reflects substantial institutional interest, although it doesn't guarantee support during market pullbacks. ABBV’s biggest risks are upcoming patent cliffs, including one for Skyrizi in 2033. Rinvoq also faces a cliff, but it's been pushed back until much later in the coming decade due to legal settlements. The offset is seven more years of Rinvoq growth and dominance, compounded by a robust pipeline that strengthens quarterly. Humira is no longer a risk. content: AbbVie Inc. ABBV raised its 2026 guidance during its third-quarter earnings call, citing sustained demand for its immunology and neuroscience treatments. Management emphasized continued growth from Skyrizi and Rinvoq, alongside expanding opportunities across its development pipeline. The discussion also addressed competitive pressures, drug pricing, regulatory milestones and commercialization timelines that could influence growth through 2027 and beyond. Chairman and CEO Robert Michael highlighted broad-based commercial momentum, supporting another upward revision to annual guidance. Third-quarter adjusted earnings reached $3.82 per share, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.74. Quote Chief commercial officer Jeffrey Stewart emphasized Skyrizi's sustained market penetration despite increasing competition. Quarterly sales reached $5.776 billion, representing 22.9% operational growth. Rinvoq generated $2.706 billion, increasing 24.3% operationally. Management raised full-year sales forecasts for both products to $21.8 billion and $10.3 billion, respectively. During questioning from JPMorgan, Stewart explained that newly approved subcutaneous Skyrizi induction for Crohn's disease could accelerate patient-share gains beginning in early 2027. Full payer access should take approximately 60 days or longer. Stewart highlighted continued demand across neuroscience, where quarterly revenues reached $3.389 billion, growing 19.5% operationally. Vraylar, Ubrelvy and Qulipta contributed to this expansion. The FDA approval of Juvmo adds another Parkinson's treatment to AbbVie's portfolio. Management expects broader Medicare coverage beginning in 2028, delaying a more significant commercial ramp. Responding to Wells Fargo, Stewart described encouraging initial physician interest in Juvmo but acknowledged near-term reimbursement limitations. Michael also identified upcoming Medicare drug-pricing changes for Vraylar as a 2027 headwind. AbbVie's Oncology Pipeline Approaches Key Milestones Chief scientific officer Roopal Thakkar highlighted positive Phase III results for etentamig in multiple myeloma. AbbVie submitted its U.S. regulatory application and anticipates an approval decision in 2027. Epkinly also demonstrated encouraging results in frontline diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, reducing the risk of disease progression or death by 51% when combined with R-CHOP. During JPMorgan and other analyst discussions, management emphasized the commercial potential of these programs. Stewart expects rapid adoption of Epkinly's frontline indication following approval, supported by its combination with an established treatment regimen. During questioning from TD Cowen, Michael addressed the dispute concerning Botox eligibility for Medicare drug-price negotiations. He cited a favorable federal district court ruling while acknowledging the government's ability to appeal. Thakkar also discussed uncertainties surrounding Rinvoq's upcoming hidradenitis suppurativa trial results. She emphasized pain reduction, disease flares and quality-of-life improvements alongside clinical response rates. Meanwhile, aesthetics revenues declined 1.8% operationally. Stewart cited continued dermal filler weakness, although improving Botox Cosmetic demand provided some support. Michael characterized future acquisitions as predominantly bolt-on transactions following the completed Apogee Therapeutics acquisition. Immunology, neuroscience, oncology and obesity remain priority areas. Reents reported approximately $14 billion in free cash flow during the first nine months, supporting continued investment and shareholder distributions.
